root_motivation: Without recording both the bytes saved by a careen sweep AND the rebuild cost it forces, the fleet has no signal to distinguish cold repos (worth careening) from hot repos (waste: reclaim 9G, pay it back in minutes). The ledger closes that feedback loop so careen-guard can make data-driven decisions.
user_persona: wintermute automation (careen-guard daemon) and Joe Yen (CLI inspection) on a developer laptop where cargo clean decisions have measurable cost.

five_whys_trace.q: Why does careen-sweep need a ledger?
five_whys_trace.a: Because careen-sweep emits per-sweep JSON but has no memory: it doesn't know whether the next build paid back what it reclaimed.

five_whys_trace.q: Why does not knowing the payback cost matter?
five_whys_trace.a: Because a hot repo rebuilt daily can recover 9G of disk, then spend it all again in recompile time within minutes, making the sweep net-negative.

five_whys_trace.q: Why can't careen-guard decide without the ledger?
five_whys_trace.a: The guard only sees instantaneous disk pressure; the signal it needs — 'did the last sweep cause a painful rebuild?' — is only observable after the sweep, across multiple build events.

acceptance_criteria.description: careen-ledger record <summary.json> appends one immutable JSONL line carrying repo, ts, removed_bytes, and classes, and prints the new entry id.
attribute <id> --rebuilt-crates N --wall-secs S appends a paired record keyed by that id with the rebuild cost; the original record is left byte-for-byte unchanged (append-only proven by a test).
verdict <repo> folds all paired records for the repo into JSON with reclaimed_bytes_total, rebuild_cost_total, and a boolean worth_careening.

The worth_careening rule is deterministic and documented: a cold-win fixture (high reclaim, low rebuild) → true; a hot-thrash fixture (low reclaim, high rebuild) → false. Two fixtures classify oppositely.
attribute can derive rebuild cost from a cargo --message-format=json build log (counting compiler-artifact lines) when --build-log <path> is given instead of explicit counts.
The ledger never rewrites or deletes a prior line; corruption of one line (bad JSON) is skipped with a warning on read, not a crash.
verdict on a repo with no history exits cleanly with an insufficient-data JSON verdict, not an error.
State path is created on first record if absent; --ledger <path> overrides the default for testing.

scope: record subcommand: ingest careen-sweep summary JSON, emit entry id
attribute subcommand: pair rebuild cost with a prior sweep record (explicit counts or cargo build log)
verdict subcommand: fold history into worth_careening recommendation
Deterministic scoring rule: reclaimed_bytes / rebuild_cost ratio vs threshold
non_goals: Automatic integration with cargo (ledger is a passive observer; caller supplies rebuild data)

additional.append_only: ledger.jsonl is append-only; no line is ever overwritten or deleted
additional.sigpipe: install sigpipe::reset() at top of main to avoid broken-pipe panics

ambiguities_resolved.question: What is the worth_careening threshold?
ambiguities_resolved.resolution: A repo is worth careening if cumulative reclaimed_bytes_total > 2 * rebuild_cost_bytes_equivalent. rebuild_cost_bytes is derived as rebuilt_crates * BYTES_PER_CRATE_COMPILE (constant 10_000_000 = ~10MB per crate-second proxy) + wall_secs * BYTES_PER_SECOND (constant 1_000_000). This is documented in the verdict output alongside the raw numbers.

ambiguities_resolved.question: What fields are required in the sweep summary JSON passed to record?
ambiguities_resolved.resolution: Required: repo (string), removed_bytes (u64), removed_entries (u64), classes (object mapping class name to count). Optional: ts (ISO-8601; defaults to now). This matches careen-sweep's output schema.
